statement: Over the unrestricted real-coefficient parameter space allowing input conics with empty real loci, the minimum number of real conics tangent to five general conics is zero.

answer.qualification: Our explicit deduction, not a quoted minimum theorem. It does not settle the minimum under the additional restriction that all five input conics have nonempty real loci.

source.location: Deduction from generic ordinary-contact locus used in Section 3; positive-definite input argument
source.version: Generic-locus source: Bachmann–Wickelgren, Section 3; deduction recorded 26 October 2026

scope: Unrestricted real-coefficient nonsingular input conics, permitting an input conic with empty real locus; regular finite covering locus.
notes:
Our explicit deduction, not a quoted minimum theorem. It does not settle the minimum under the additional restriction that all five input conics have nonempty real loci.

Source discussion. The exact minimum is zero over the unrestricted real-coefficient parameter space. Choose one input conic with positive-definite quadratic form, hence empty real locus. At a regular generic solution, tangency to each input is a unique ordinary contact. A real solution would have its unique contact with the definite conic fixed by conjugation, hence real, a contradiction. Positive definiteness is Euclidean open and meets the generic covering locus.
